jobs.title: Fleet Finance Director
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Job Overview:

Primoris Services Corporation is seeking a strategic, data-driven Director of Fleet Finance, Analytics & Audit to lead financial management, analytics, audit governance, and performance optimization for the corporate fleet organization. Reporting to the Senior Fleet Operations Director, this leader will partner with Operations, Fleet Management, Procurement, Project Controls, and Corporate Finance to improve profitability, strengthen internal controls, drive compliance, and deliver actionable business intelligence. The ideal candidate brings expertise in finance, accounting, audit, business analytics, financial modeling, and operational performance management , with the ability to transform complex fleet data into strategic business decisions.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Business Partnership
- Serve as the primary finance, analytics, and compliance advisor to Fleet and Operations leadership.
- Partner with Business Unit leaders to support fleet utilization, capital investments, asset replacement strategies, and operational performance.
- Lead and develop finance and cost control personnel while fostering accountability, continuous improvement, and data integrity.
- Support strategic decision-making through financial insights and performance analysis.

Finance, Analytics & Business Intelligence
- Develop executive dashboards, KPIs, and performance reporting.
- Analyze fleet utilization, maintenance costs, fuel spending, downtime, lifecycle costs, accident trends, and operational efficiency.
- Conduct variance analysis, forecasting, trend analysis, and financial modeling to identify risks and cost-saving opportunities.
- Develop predictive analytics and capital planning models to optimize fleet investments and replacement schedules.
- Ensure accuracy and integrity of fleet financial and operational data.

Audit, Compliance & Internal Controls
- Lead internal and external fleet-related audit activities.
- Design and monitor internal controls to strengthen financial compliance and operational governance.
- Conduct reviews of fleet purchases, maintenance spending, fuel transactions, P-card activity, vendor billing, and utilization practices.
- Identify control gaps, compliance risks, and process deficiencies and implement corrective actions.
- Ensure compliance with GAAP, corporate policies, regulatory requirements, and governance standards.

Budgeting, Forecasting & Strategic Planning
- Lead annual operating and capital budget development, long-range financial planning, and capital replacement forecasting.
- Prepare monthly and quarterly performance reviews, forecasts, and executive presentations.
- Evaluate ROI, total cost of ownership (TCO), and business cases for major fleet investments and strategic initiatives.
- Monitor financial performance, investigate variances, and support corrective action plans.

Strategic Initiatives
- Lead fleet cost optimization initiatives and operational performance improvement programs.
- Support acquisitions, due diligence, integration planning, and vendor evaluations.
- Partner with Procurement to assess supplier performance, pricing compliance, and contract effectiveness.
- Provide financial support for major projects, bids, and corporate initiatives.

Qualifications:

Required
- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Analytics, or related field.
- 5+ years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, audit, analytics, or financial planning and analysis.
- 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams and cross-functional stakeholders.
- Strong knowledge of GAAP, internal controls, auditing principles, financial reporting, budgeting, and forecasting.
- Advanced skills in financial modeling, business intelligence, data analytics, and Microsoft Excel.
- Experience with ERP systems, reporting platforms, and executive-level presentations.
- Excellent communication, problem-solving, and process improvement skills.
- Experience in construction, industrial services, transportation, fleet, equipment, or other asset-intensive industries preferred.

Preferred
- CPA, CMA, CIA, MBA, or comparable professional certification.
- Experience in public accounting, internal audit, SOX compliance, or operational audits.
- Expertise with Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or similar analytics platforms.
- Fleet, transportation, equipment, or asset management industry experience.

Company Overview:

Primoris Services Corporation is a premier specialty contractor providing critical infrastructure services to the utility, energy, and renewables markets throughout the United States and Canada. Built on a foundation of trust, we deliver a range of engineering, construction, and maintenance services that power, connect, and enhance society. On projects spanning utility-scale solar, renewables, power delivery, communications, and transportation infrastructure, we offer unmatched value to our clients, a safe and entrepreneurial culture to our employees, and innovation and excellence to our communities. To learn more, visit www.prim.com and follow us on social media at @PrimorisServicesCorporation.
Benefits:

- 10 paid holidays

jobs.title: Construction Analytics, Data & Power BI Manager - Primoris Energy Services
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Position Summary
The Construction Analytics, Data & Power BI Manager is responsible for developing, maintaining, and governing construction-focused analytics, dashboards, and reporting solutions that support project execution and leadership decision-making across Primoris Energy Services.
This role transforms data from field, project, and corporate systems into clear, actionable insights related to cost, schedule, productivity, and performance. Operating within a matrix organization, the Manager partners closely with Operations, Project Controls, Construction Technology, Finance, and leadership teams to ensure data is accurate, consistent, and aligned with how projects are delivered in the field.

Key Responsibilities
Construction Analytics & Reporting
- Own and manage construction analytics and reporting solutions across all divisions.
- Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards supporting project performance, executive reporting, and operational insights.
- Translate complex construction data into clear, usable information for project teams and leadership.
- Ensure analytics focus on execution performance—not just compliance reporting.

Data Integration & Data Quality
- Partner with the Construction Technology Manager and IT to integrate data from field and enterprise systems, including: - EcoSys
- Viewpoint
- Autodesk Construction Cloud
- Power Apps
- SharePoint
- Access databases

- Establish and enforce data definitions, standards, and governance to ensure consistency across projects and divisions.
- Monitor data quality and resolve issues impacting reporting accuracy or usability.

Project Performance & Insights
- Support analysis of project metrics such as: - Cost performance and forecasting
- Schedule trends and variance
- Labor productivity and production rates
- Risk indicators and early warning signals

- Partner with Project Controls, Operations, and Finance to align analytics with business needs.
- Help leadership identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement across projects.

Power BI Development & Enablement
- Design scalable Power BI models, datasets, and visualizations.
- Manage report versioning, access controls, and user experience.
- Support training and adoption of analytics tools across field and office teams.
- Enable self-service analytics where appropriate while maintaining data integrity.

Governance, Standards & Continuous Improvement
- Establish best practices for construction analytics, reporting cadence, and dashboard usage.
- Prevent fragmentation of reporting tools and “shadow dashboards.”
- Continuously improve analytics capabilities based on user feedback and evolving business needs.
- Support audits, executive reviews, and strategic initiatives with reliable data.

Collaboration & Matrix Leadership
- Operate effectively within a matrix organization, influencing project and division teams without direct authority.
- Work closely with: - Director of Technical Services
- Construction Technology Manager
- Project Controls
- Operations leadership
- Finance and corporate stakeholders

- Communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences.

Qualifications
Required
- Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Data Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
- 7+ years of experience in construction analytics, project controls, data analytics, or related roles within construction or infrastructure.
- Advanced experience with Power BI, including data modeling and dashboard development.
- Strong understanding of construction execution, project controls, and field data workflows.
- Experience working with construction and enterprise systems such as EcoSys, Viewpoint, or Autodesk Construction Cloud.
- Ability to translate operational questions into meaningful analytics and insights.

Preferred
- Experience supporting multiple construction divisions or market sectors.
- Familiarity with SQL, Power Platform, or similar data tools.
- Experience aligning analytics across Operations, Project Controls, and Finance.
- Background in a large, diversified contractor or EPC organization.

Working Conditions
- Office-based role located in Houston / Pearland, TX , with occasional jobsite visits.
- Periodic travel to active construction projects as needed.
- Exposure to active construction environments during site visits.
- Must comply with all Primoris safety policies and procedures.

#LI-CM1

Company Overview:

Primoris Energy Services is a major direct-hire contractor in the U.S. delivering self-performed turnkey industrial construction and EPC services. We offer these services to our clients within the refining, gas processing, chemical/petrochemical, hydrogen, power generation, mining, pulp and paper industries from the first groundbreaking activity all the way through commissioning and start-up of the project. Primoris forms a partnership with our customers and major stakeholders from early-stage engineering through construction completion and commercial operation, safely, on-time, and within budget.

jobs.title: Strategic Sourcing Specialist II
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Position Summary
The Strategic Sourcing Specialist II independently executes sourcing and procurement activities for materials, equipment, and services supporting utility-scale solar and battery energy storage (BESS) projects. This role partners with supply chain leaders, engineering, estimating, construction, operations, project management, and suppliers to develop sourcing strategies, lead competitive sourcing events, evaluate supplier capabilities, negotiate commercial terms, manage supplier performance, and mitigate supply chain risk.
The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and commercial judgment with demonstrated sourcing experience, can manage multiple assignments with limited direction, and is prepared to own defined commodities, supplier relationships, or project procurement scopes.

Primary Responsibilities
Supplier Identification & Qualification
- Identify, research, qualify, and recommend suppliers for assigned commodities, projects, and business requirements.
- Lead supplier capability assessments, reference checks, financial reviews, and preliminary risk evaluations.
- Coordinate supplier onboarding and maintain accurate approved-supplier records and qualification documentation.
- Analyze market trends, supplier economics, emerging technologies, and capacity constraints affecting solar, BESS, electrical, and construction-related commodities.

RFx Support & Competitive Bidding
- Develop and administer RFx events from scope definition through award recommendation.
- Coordinate bid schedules, supplier communications, clarifications, and cross-functional technical and commercial evaluations.
- Perform bid normalization, total-cost-of-ownership analysis, and comparisons of pricing, lead time, technical compliance, quality, capacity, risk, and commercial terms.
- Prepare and present fact-based sourcing recommendations, negotiation strategies, and award analyses for approval.

Contract Negotiation & Commercial Management
- Lead supplier contract negotiations covering pricing, payment, delivery, warranty, indemnity, limitation of liability, termination, and other commercial terms within delegated authority, escalating material business or legal risks as needed.
- Prepare bid tabulations, negotiation plans, commercial summaries, purchase recommendations, and contract documentation.
- Review, negotiate, and redline supplier agreements using approved templates and contracting standards; engage Legal, Finance, Risk, Quality, or project stakeholders for material exceptions or specialized guidance.
- Identify, quantify, document, and mitigate commercial and supply chain risks, including pricing, tariffs, logistics, capacity, schedule, warranty, and contractual exposure.

Supplier Relationship Management
- Own day-to-day relationships with assigned suppliers and serve as the commercial point of contact for defined commodities or project scopes.
- Resolve supplier issues involving pricing, delivery, quality, documentation, and contractual commitments, escalating when business impact warrants.
- Lead supplier meetings, performance reviews, and business updates using defined KPIs, scorecards, and corrective-action plans.
- Drive supplier improvement, cost-reduction, resilience, and continuity initiatives and track actions through completion.

Procurement Analytics & Reporting
- Maintain accurate supplier, pricing, contract, savings, and procurement records within company systems.
- Develop spend analyses, sourcing dashboards, vendor scorecards, and supplier performance reports for assigned scopes.
- Perform cost benchmarking, should-cost or total-cost analysis, market intelligence, and validated savings tracking.
- Translate demand forecasts, project schedules, and market data into sourcing actions and supply recommendations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Partner with Engineering, Estimating, Operations, Construction, Quality, Logistics, Finance, Legal, and Project Management to define requirements and execute sourcing plans.
- Interpret technical specifications, drawings, scopes of work, and commercial requirements to support supplier selection and procurement decisions.
- Provide clear procurement status, forecast, risk, and decision updates to project teams and sourcing leadership.
- Lead or implement process improvements that increase sourcing efficiency, data quality, cost control, and supplier performance.

Compliance & Risk Management
- Ensure sourcing activities comply with company policies, delegated authority, supplier standards, contractual obligations, and applicable regulatory requirements.
- Monitor supplier performance related to safety, quality, delivery, sustainability, trade compliance, and other project requirements.
- Maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready sourcing and procurement documentation.
- Develop and track mitigation plans for supplier capacity, pricing, logistics, geopolitical, material-availability, and single-source risks.

Other Duties
- Perform additional sourcing, procurement, and supply chain responsibilities as assigned.
- Travel as necessary to supplier facilities, project sites, and industry events.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Construction Management, Engineering, Finance, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
- 3-5 years of progressive experience in procurement, purchasing, strategic sourcing, supply chain, construction, manufacturing, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience independently administering competitive bids, performing commercial analysis, managing suppliers, and negotiating supplier contracts and commercial terms.
- Strong analytical, organizational, project-management, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to make fact-based recommendations.
- Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and working proficiency with other Microsoft Office applications.
- Ability to independently manage multiple sourcing activities, competing deadlines, and changing priorities in a project environment.
- Strong written, verbal, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience sourcing equipment, materials, or services for utility-scale solar, BESS, electrical, EPC, construction, manufacturing, or energy projects.
- Experience developing RFx packages, evaluating total cost of ownership, and negotiating supplier agreements involving commercial and contractual terms.
- Working knowledge of supply markets, contract principles, supplier-risk management, logistics, and trade or regulatory requirements.
- Experience using ERP, e-sourcing, procurement, contract-management, or supplier-performance systems.
- Familiarity with technical specifications, construction drawings, electrical equipment, renewable energy technologies, or major capital projects.
- CPSM, CSCP, CPIM, or other relevant supply chain certification.

Key Competencies
- Commercial Judgment
- Strategic Sourcing Execution
- Supplier Relationship and Performance Management
- Negotiation and Contracting
- Total Cost and Data Analysis
- Supply Market Intelligence
- Risk Identification and Mitigation
- Cross-Functional Influence
- Project and Priority Management
- Decision Quality and Accountability
- Continuous Improvement
- Professional Communication

Target Salary 80-100K

Company Overview:

Primoris Renewable Energy, a business within Primoris Services Corporation’s Energy segment, is a leading power generation engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) provider specializing in utility and commercial scale solar power, energy storage, solar repower, and operations and maintenance. Standing at the forefront of energy transformation, we are dedicated to doing the right thing for our customers, people, and planet – shaping a more sustainable future for generations to come.

jobs.title: Director Risk Management
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Director Risk Management
Summary
The Director of Risk Management is responsible for leading the development, implementation, and ongoing management of Primoris’ risk management strategy. This position provides strategic direction and operational oversight across enterprise risk, insurance, claims, surety, contractual risk, and loss prevention programs. The role partners closely with executive leadership, operations, finance, legal, safety, fleet, human resources, insurance brokers, carriers, and project teams to identify, evaluate, and mitigate operational, financial, contractual, legal, safety, environmental, and insurance-related risks.
The Director of Risk Management serves as a key advisor to business leaders, providing practical risk guidance that supports company growth, protects company assets, improves project performance, strengthens compliance, and reduces the total cost of risk.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Risk Management
- Develop, implement, and continuously improve risk management programs, policies, and processes that support company strategy, operational objectives, and business continuity.
- Identify, assess, and monitor risk exposures across business operations, projects, contracts, insurance programs, financial structures, safety, fleet, environmental matters, and business continuity planning.
- Provide guidance and recommendations to executive leadership and business decision-makers regarding risk mitigation strategies, emerging exposures, and program improvements.
- Establish and monitor key risk indicators, loss trends, and risk-related reporting to support informed decision-making.
- Evaluate current and proposed business operations, processes, structures, and risk exposures to identify areas of potential loss, disruption, or financial impact.
- Lead, mentor, and develop risk and claims personnel to ensure the effective operation of the function.

Insurance Program Management
- Manage the company’s insurance portfolio, including but not limited to: - General Liability
- Builders Risk
- Professional Liability
- Workers’ Compensation
- Commercial Auto
- Umbrella/Excess Liability
- Pollution Liability

- Lead annual insurance renewal activities in partnership with brokers, carriers, underwriters, finance, legal, and operational leaders.
- Evaluate coverage terms, limits, retentions, premiums, exclusions, and program structure to ensure alignment with company risk profile and project needs.
- Manage Builders Risk placements, including project-specific and blanket programs, ensuring coverage is appropriate for project scope, value, and contractual requirements.
- Coordinate insurance audits, premium reviews, exposure reporting, and resolution of discrepancies with carriers and brokers.
- Benchmark insurance coverage, retentions, premiums, and program structure against industry practices and recommend adjustments as appropriate.

Claims Management
- Oversee the claims management process across all lines of coverage, ensuring timely reporting, investigation, reserve review, and resolution.
- Provide leadership and direction to claims team members, third-party administrators, insurers, brokers, and defense counsel to support effective claims handling and cost control.
- Partner with legal, operations, safety, fleet, and project teams on complex, high-exposure, or litigated claims.
- Analyze claims data to identify loss trends, root causes, recurring exposures, and opportunities for corrective action.
- Monitor claim reserves, claim development, litigation strategy, and overall claims performance.
- Report significant claim activity, loss trends, and recommended mitigation actions to senior leadership.

Alternative Risk Financing
- Evaluate risk financing strategies, including large deductible programs, self-insurance, loss-sensitive programs, funded retentions, fronting arrangements, captive insurance structures, and other alternative risk transfer options.
- Partner with internal stakeholders and external advisors, including brokers, actuaries, legal counsel, captive managers, and consultants, to assess feasibility and financial impact of alternative risk structures.
- Develop and review financial models related to risk retention, total cost of risk, cash flow impact, reserve adequacy, and long-term program sustainability.
- Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, reporting, licensing, and governance requirements related to alternative risk financing programs.

Surety Bond Program Management
- Oversee the company’s surety bonding program, including bid bonds, performance bonds, payment bonds, and related surety requirements.
- Monitor bonding capacity, aggregate exposure, project backlog, and future business needs to ensure adequate surety support for company growth.
- Maintain strong relationships with surety partners and proactively manage the company’s surety credit profile.
- Coordinate with finance, treasury, operations, and executive leadership to provide timely financial and operational information to sureties.
- Negotiate favorable bond terms, rates, collateral requirements, and program structure where appropriate.

Contractual Risk Review
- Review and provide guidance on risk-related contract provisions, including insurance requirements, indemnity, limitation of liability, waiver of subrogation, additional insured language, bonding requirements, and other risk transfer provisions.
- Support legal, operations, estimating, procurement, and project teams in evaluating risk terms within owner contracts, subcontracts, vendor agreements, supplier agreements, equipment leases, joint ventures, and professional services agreements.
- Identify contract terms that may create elevated financial, operational, insurance, or compliance risk and recommend appropriate revisions or mitigation strategies.
- Ensure contractual insurance and risk requirements are aligned with company policies, insurance program capabilities, and project-specific exposures.

Safety, Fleet, and Loss Prevention Partnership
- Partner with Safety, Fleet, Operations, and project leadership to reduce the frequency and severity of losses across Workers’ Compensation, General Liability, Auto Liability, and other lines of coverage.
- Translate claims data, incident trends, and loss drivers into actionable recommendations for safety programs, fleet initiatives, training, and field-level corrective actions.
- Collaborate with Fleet leadership on auto liability and physical damage exposures, driver qualification standards, vehicle maintenance protocols, telematics programs, and accident response procedures.
- Participate in regular reviews of claims trends, incident patterns, high-severity exposures, near-miss data, and loss prevention opportunities.
- Quantify the financial impact of safety and fleet loss reduction initiatives on insurance costs, experience modification factors, and total cost of risk.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Risk Culture
- Serve as a proactive risk management resource to business units and corporate functions, including operations, preconstruction, estimating, finance, legal, safety, fleet, human resources, procurement, and project teams.
- Educate and advise project managers, operational leaders, and other stakeholders on risk management practices, insurance obligations, claims reporting, and loss prevention.
- Promote a practical, risk-aware culture that supports sound decision-making without creating unnecessary barriers to business execution.
- Coordinate with Finance and Accounting on risk-related financial reporting, reserve analysis, insurance accruals, and total cost of risk reporting.
- Support business continuity, disaster recovery, health and safety, security, and compliance initiatives as needed.

Minimum Qualifications
- 10+ years of progressive experience in risk management, insurance, claims, contracts, legal compliance, project management, or a related function.
- Experience supporting construction, infrastructure, energy, industrial, commercial, heavy civil, utility, renewable energy, or specialty contracting operations.
- Experience working with large general contractors, EPC firms, construction management firms, specialty contractors, or similarly complex project-based organizations.
- Demonstrated experience managing commercial insurance programs across multiple lines of coverage.
- Experience overseeing claims management and loss mitigation across Workers’ Compensation, General Liability, Auto Liability, Builders Risk, and other relevant lines.
- Experience working with insurance brokers, carriers, sureties, third-party administrators, actuaries, legal counsel, and internal business leaders.
- Strong understanding of construction operations, project risk, contractual risk transfer, insurance requirements, and claims processes.
- Ability to lead teams, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and communicate complex risk topics clearly to executive and operational audiences.

Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Construction Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Finance, Insurance, or a related field required.
- Master’s degree, MBA, or advanced degree in Risk Management, Finance, Business, or related field preferred.

Preferred Certifications
- Construction Risk and Insurance Specialist (CRIS)
- Associate in Risk Management (ARM)
- Certified Risk Manager (CRM)
- Chartered Property Casualty Underwriter (CPCU)
- Certified Construction Professional or related construction/risk designation preferred

Skills and Competencies
- Strong strategic, analytical, and financial acumen with the ability to evaluate risk exposure, total cost of risk, insurance program economics, reserves, and loss trends.
- Ability to translate complex risk, insurance, claims, and contractual concepts into practical business recommendations.
- Strong executive communication skills with the ability to present risk issues, program updates, and recommendations to senior leadership.
- Deep understanding of construction risk, project delivery models, contractual risk transfer, and operational exposures.
- Strong negotiation skills with brokers, carriers, sureties, vendors, contract counterparties, and external advisors.
- Demonstrated ability to partner across functions and influence outcomes without direct authority.
- Proficiency with risk management information systems, claims management platforms, data analytics tools, and Microsoft Office applications.

Work Authorization
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Primoris does not provide sponsorship for this position now or in the future.

On projects spanning utility-scale solar, renewables, power delivery, communications, and transportation infrastructure, we offer unmatched value to our clients, a safe and entrepreneurial culture to our employees, and innovation and excellence to our communities. jobs.title: Procurement Manager - Primoris Heavy Civil - Louisiana
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Job Summary

The Procurement Manager for Primoris Heavy Civil in Louisiana will be responsible for overseeing and managing all procurement activities for assigned heavy civil construction projects in the region. This role focuses on strategic sourcing, vendor management, and ensuring cost-effective and timely acquisition of materials, equipment, and services to support project success.

Job Responsibilities

* Develop and implement procurement strategies tailored to heavy civil construction projects in Louisiana, including but not limited to earthworks, marine construction, and infrastructure development.
* Manage the end-to-end procurement process, from requisition to purchase order, ensuring compliance with company policies and project specifications.
* Identify, evaluate, and qualify new and existing suppliers, subcontractors, and vendors, conducting thorough due diligence and performance reviews.
* Negotiate favorable terms, conditions, and pricing with suppliers to achieve cost savings and optimize project budgets.
* Prepare and issue Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and invitations to bid, analyzing responses and making recommendations.
* Collaborate closely with project managers, estimators, and engineering teams to understand project needs and material specifications.
* Monitor supplier performance, resolve delivery or quality issues, and manage supplier relationships effectively.
* Ensure timely delivery of materials and services to support project schedules and prevent delays.
* Maintain accurate procurement records, contracts, and documentation.
* Stay informed of market trends, material availability, and regulatory changes impacting the heavy civil construction industry.
* Implement and enforce Primoris Services Corporation's safety and ethical guidelines within the procurement function.

Job Qualifications

* Minimum of 7-10 years of progressive experience in procurement, with a significant portion in the heavy civil construction industry.
* Proven track record of managing large-scale procurement for complex heavy civil projects.
* Strong knowledge of construction materials, equipment, and services relevant to heavy civil projects (e.g., aggregates, concrete, steel, earthmoving equipment, marine services).
* Expertise in contract negotiation, vendor management, and supply chain optimization.
* Proficiency in procurement software and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle).
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
* Strong communication, interpersonal, and leadership abilities.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

* Professional certification (e.g., CPSM, C.P.M.) is a plus.

#LI-KG1

Primoris Heavy Civil provides highway, port, airfield, rail and marine (intermodal transportation) construction services to private commercial and industrial clients as well as governmental entities such as the Department of Transportation and the US Army Corps of Engineers. jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Job Overview
The Electrical Program Manager (Master Electrician) will serve as the named license holder on PES’s contractor license and will lead the development, implementation, and oversight of the company’s electrical program. This role ensures compliance with all electrical codes and licensing requirements while creating a scalable program that supports operational excellence, workforce development, and safe execution of electrical scopes across PES projects. The position will be based out of the PES Houston office , with travel required approximately one week per month or as project needs dictate.

Key Responsibilities
Licensing & Compliance
- Serve as the designated Master Electrician on PES’s contractor license.
- Acquire and maintain active Master Electrician licenses in every state where PES currently performs work or secures future projects.
- Ensure company-wide compliance with federal, state, and local electrical codes, permitting, and licensing regulations.
- Oversee inspections, audits, and interface with regulatory authorities.
- Maintain current knowledge of NEC, NFPA, OSHA, and jurisdictional requirements.

Program Development
- Develop, implement, and maintain PES’s electrical program , including standards, procedures, QA/QC, and best practices for all electrical work.
- Establish training, apprenticeship, and certification paths for PES electricians.
- Create and maintain documentation for safety, compliance, and operational processes.

Project Oversight
- Provide technical expertise and oversight for electrical scopes on PES projects.
- Review project drawings, specifications, and submittals to ensure compliance and constructability.
- Support project managers and site managers with troubleshooting, design clarifications, and problem resolution.
- Participate in project planning, estimating, and resource allocation for electrical work.

Leadership & Training
- Mentor electricians, foremen, and supervisors in PES’s standards and electrical code compliance.
- Track and verify apprentice and journeyman hours.
- Lead continuing education, skills development, and safety programs for the electrical workforce.
- Conduct periodic site visits and audits to verify compliance and performance.
- Support recruitment, retention, and development of licensed electricians to sustain growth.

Qualifications
- Active Master Electrician license in Texas and ability to acquire/maintain Master Electrician licenses in all states where PES performs or secures projects .
- 10+ years of progressive experience in electrical construction , with emphasis on industrial, utility, or power generation projects .
- Direct experience with Power Generation and Industrial New Construction, gas turbines, switchgear, substations, and high-voltage systems preferred.
- Proven ability to build and manage electrical safety, compliance, and training programs.
- Strong knowledge of NEC, NFPA 70E, OSHA, and local/state code requirements.
- Effective leadership, mentoring, and communication skills.
- Proficiency in project management and construction management software (Procore, MS Project, Primavera, or equivalent).
- Based in Houston, TX , with the ability to travel approximately one week per month (or more as project needs require).

What This Role Offers
- Opportunity to shape and lead PES’s company-wide electrical program .
- Competitive compensation and benefits package.
- Career growth within a leading construction and energy services company.

Company Overview:

Primoris Energy Services is a major direct-hire contractor in the U.S. delivering self-performed turnkey industrial construction and EPC services. We offer these services to our clients within the refining, gas processing, chemical/petrochemical, hydrogen, power generation, mining, pulp and paper industries from the first groundbreaking activity all the way through commissioning and start-up of the project. Primoris forms a partnership with our customers and major stakeholders from early-stage engineering through construction completion and commercial operation, safely, on-time, and within budget.
Benefits:

- Competitive compensation, paid weekly.

- Best-in-class medical, dental, vision, and LTD/STD coverage.

- 401(k) with company match, vested on day one.

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan [ESPP].

- Pet coverage for your furry friends.

- Legal assistance coverage.

- Award-winning safety programs.
